page.title: Integrations | AgentMesh
page.description: Send the mesh's traces to the tracing tool you already use, screen messages with the screening service you trust, and keep each agent's code on GitHub.
page.h1: Plug the mesh into the tools you already run
page.lede: Each card says how far we have taken it. Tested by us means we ran it against the live service. Speaks the standard means the product accepts an open standard the mesh uses, but we have not tried that product. Written from the vendor's documentation means we followed the vendor's instructions and have not run it live yet.

standard.label: Speaks the standard; not tested by us

vendor-docs.label: Written from the vendor's documentation, not yet tested

groups.title: Send traces to the tool you already watch
groups.intro: The mesh publishes each hop between agents as an OpenTelemetry span, so those hops show up next to the traces your own services already produce.

cards.name: Any OpenTelemetry collector
cards.line: Send spans to your collector, and it forwards them to whatever you run.

cards.name: Google Cloud Trace
cards.line: One export command sends spans directly to Google Cloud Trace.

cards.name: Azure Application Insights
cards.line: A collector you run holds your Azure credential and forwards spans to Application Insights.

cards.name: Honeycomb
cards.line: Honeycomb accepts OpenTelemetry data. Send the export to its endpoint, or to your collector.

cards.name: Datadog
cards.line: Datadog accepts OpenTelemetry data. Send the export to its endpoint, or to your collector.

cards.name: Grafana Tempo
cards.line: Tempo accepts OpenTelemetry data. Send the export to its endpoint, or to your collector.

cards.name: New Relic
cards.line: New Relic accepts OpenTelemetry data. Send the export to its endpoint, or to your collector.

groups.title: Screen messages with the service you trust
groups.intro: Before a message reaches your agent, the node can ask a screening service to check it, through one documented interface we call the screening socket. You keep your own policy and your own key.

cards.name: Google Model Armor
cards.line: The node calls Model Armor directly, using the screening template you set up in your Google Cloud project.

cards.name: Azure AI Content Safety
cards.line: A small function in your Azure subscription passes each message from the node to Content Safety.
cards.setup: A function in your subscription, connected to the screening socket

cards.name: Lakera Guard
cards.line: The node has a Lakera Guard setting, built from Lakera's documentation.

cards.name: Your own screener
cards.line: Build a service that answers the screening socket, and the node will send it each message to check.

groups.title: Keep your agent's code on GitHub
groups.intro: Install the AgentMesh app on your GitHub account, and each of your agents gets its own repository there.

cards.name: GitHub
cards.line: Each agent's code lives in a repository under your own account.
cards.setup: Install the AgentMesh app on your account
